business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business.
business_model.claim: Wabash National Corporation designs, manufactures, and services trailers, truck bodies, structural composite panels, aerodynamic solutions, specialty food grade processing equipment, and parts and services including Trailers as a Service.
quotes: To that end, we design, manufacture, and service a diverse range of products supporting first-to-final mile operations, including dry freight and refrigerated trailers, platform trailers, tank trailers, dry and refrigerated truck bodies, structural composite panels and products, trailer aerodynamic solutions, and specialty food grade processing equipment.
In addition, through Wabash Hub, customers gain access to a nationwide parts and service network, Trailers as a Service (TaaS)℠, and advanced tools designed to streamline operations and drive growth.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business.
business_model.claim: Wabash manages its business through the Transportation Solutions and Parts & Services operating and reportable segments.
quotes: Based on how the Chief Operating Decision Maker (“CODM”) manages the business, allocates resources, makes operating decisions, and evaluates operating performance, the Company manages its business in two operating and reportable segments: Transportation Solutions (“TS”) and Parts & Services (“P&S”).

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business.
business_model.claim: The Transportation Solutions segment designs and manufactures dry and refrigerated van trailers, platform trailers, tank trailers, truck-mounted tanks, truck bodies, and wood flooring.
quotes: The TS segment comprises the design and manufacturing operations for the Company’s transportation-related equipment and products.
This includes dry and refrigerated van trailers, platform trailers, and the Company’s wood flooring production facility.
Additionally, the TS segment includes tank trailers and truck-mounted tanks.
Finally, truck-mounted dry and refrigerated bodies, as well as service and stake bodies, are also included in the TS segment.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business.
business_model.claim: The Parts & Services segment encompasses aftermarket parts and services, truck body upfitting solutions, DuraPlate composite panels beyond semi-trailers, engineered stainless-steel storage tanks and mixers, Wabash Parts LLC, Linq Venture Holdings LLC, and Trailers as a Service.
quotes: The P&S segment comprises the Company’s Parts & Services business, as well as the Upfitting Solutions and Services business (a component of our Truck Bodies business).
Additionally, the Company’s Composites business, which focuses on the use of DuraPlate® composite panels beyond the semi-trailer market, is also part of the P&S segment.
Finally, the P&S segment includes the Company’s Engineered Products business, which manufactures stainless-steel storage tanks and silos, mixers and processors for a variety of end markets.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: Prior to intersegment eliminations in 2025, Transportation Solutions generated $1,344.4 million of net sales compared to $237.1 million for Parts & Services.
quotes: TS segment sales, prior to the elimination of intersegment sales, were $1,344.4 million in 2025, a decrease of $410.8 million, or 23.4% compared to 2024.
P&S segment sales, prior to the elimination of intersegment sales, were $237.1 million in 2025, an increase of $32.1 million, or 15.6%, compared to 2024.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A and the Q3 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: In the third quarter of 2026, Parts & Services achieved a 15.7% gross profit margin and $5.8 million in operating income, whereas Transportation Solutions posted a 1.0% gross profit margin and a $7.5 million operating loss.
quotes: Gross profit, prior to the elimination of intersegment sales, as a percentage of net sales, was 15.7% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 17.4% in the 2025 period.
Operating income for the quarter amounted to $5.8 million, or 8.3% of sales.
Gross profit, prior to the elimination of intersegment sales, as a percentage of net sales, was 1.0% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to 1.5% in the comparative 2025 period.
Operating loss for the quarter amounted to $7.5 million, representing 1.8% of sales.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business.
business_model.claim: Wabash serves customers across transportation, logistics, and infrastructure markets, while its tank trailers and engineered products serve broader end markets including dairy, food and beverage, pharmaceutical, chemical, craft brewing, biotech, and specialty vehicles.
quotes: Today we combine physical and digital technologies to deliver innovative, end-to-end solutions that optimize supply chains across transportation, logistics, and infrastructure markets.

The customers and end markets that these components serve are broader and more diverse than the van and platform trailer industries, including the dairy, food and beverage, pharmaceutical, chemical, craft brewing, biotech, and specialty vehicle markets.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: The company sells through longstanding relationships with core customers as well as an extensive dealer and preferred partner network.
quotes: We believe our position as a leader in our key industries is the result of longstanding relationships with our core customers, our demonstrated ability to attract new customers, our broad and innovative product lines, our engineering leadership, and our extensive dealer and preferred partner network.
Our Wabash Parts joint venture rapidly established significant distribution capabilities that allow our dealer network efficient access to our comprehensive portfolio of aftermarket parts.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Risk Factors.
business_model.claim: In 2025, Wabash's five largest customers accounted for approximately 35% of aggregate net sales, while no individual customer accounted for more than 10% and international sales were below that share.
quotes: Furthermore, we are subject to a concentration of risk as our five largest customers together accounted for approximately 35% of our aggregate net sales in 2025.
No individual customer accounted for more than 10% of our aggregate net sales in 2025 and international sales accounted for less than 10% in 2025.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business, Item 1A Risk Factors, and Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: Revenue in the trailer business is driven directly by freight volumes, broader U.S. economic conditions, and trucking carrier profitability, which affects carriers' ability to buy new trailers.
quotes: Trailer demand is a direct function of the amount of freight to be transported.

Trucking company profitability, which can be influenced by factors such as fuel prices, freight tonnage volumes, and government regulations, is highly correlated with the overall economy of the U.S.; carrier profitability significantly impacts demand for, and the financial ability to, purchase new trailers.

Demand for our products is sensitive to changes in economic conditions, including changes related to unemployment, consumer confidence and income, new housing starts, industrial production, inflationary pressures, government regulations such as federal hours-of-service rules, truck safety, limitations on vehicle weight, size, and configuration, and federal emissions standards.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Quarterly revenue fluctuates with unit shipment volumes across product lines; in the third quarter of 2026, net sales rose 24.8% as new trailer shipments increased 43.3% to 9,563 units, outweighing a 45.1% drop in new truck body shipments to 1,685 units.
quotes: Net sales in the third quarter of 2026, increased $94.8 million, or 24.8%, compared to the third quarter of 2025.

New trailers shipped during the third quarter of 2026 totaled 9,563 trailers compared to 6,675 trailers in the prior year period, an increase of 43.3%, which was primarily driven by higher dry van and platform shipments partially offset by lower tank trailer shipments.

New truck bodies shipped during the third quarter of 2026 totaled 1,685 truck bodies compared to 3,067 truck bodies in the prior year period, a decrease of 45.1% attributable to continued softened demand.
The growth in revenue from new trailer shipments outpaced the reduction in revenue from lower truck body shipments.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 7 MD&A, and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Wabash is growing its Parts & Services, upfitting, Trailers as a Service, and digital marketplace businesses to expand recurring, less cyclical revenue and partially offset trailer manufacturing cycles.
quotes: By growing our more recurring revenue business, we expect to achieve a larger base of less cyclical sales and profit to provide a more meaningful offset to the cycles we’ve historically seen in our Transportation Solutions business.

The overall increase in sales for this segment was due primarily to the growth of our Upfitting centers and our Trailers as a Service (TaaS)℠ offerings, which combined grew by $24.7 million compared to 2024.

The overall increase in sales for this segment was primarily due to higher sales within our upfit and services businesses of approximately $9.1 million and Process Systems of approximately $1.6 million, partially offset by lower sales within our Aftermarket Parts business of $1.8 million due to decreased demand.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 earnings release and Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Risk Factors.
business_model.claim: Customer order backlog provides near-term production visibility, standing at approximately $1,198 million at the end of the third quarter of 2026, though cancellations and unfairly traded trailer imports can reduce realized revenue.
quotes: As of September 30, 2026, total Company backlog stood at approximately $1,198 million, an increase of $242 million over the prior quarter.
Our backlog represents future production for which we have written orders from our customers that have defined delivery timeframes.
Orders that comprise our backlog may be subject to changes in quantities, delivery, specifications and terms, or cancellation.

Imports subject to these proceedings have adversely affected, and may continue to adversely affect, the U.S. trailer industry, including domestic production, shipments, financial performance and employment.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A and 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
business_model.claim: Cost of sales comprises variable material costs and fixed and variable manufacturing expenses—including direct and indirect labor, outbound freight, overhead, and depreciation—making gross margins sensitive to commodity volatility and limited supplier bases.
quotes: Cost of sales is comprised of material costs, a variable expense, and other manufacturing costs, comprised of both fixed and variable expenses, including direct and indirect labor, outbound freight, overhead expenses, and depreciation.

We currently rely on a limited number of suppliers for raw materials and key components in the manufacturing of our products, such as tires, landing gear, axles, suspensions, specialty steel coil, stainless steel, plastic, aluminum and lumber.

In addition, price volatility and changes in the availability of commodities we purchase, which have fluctuated significantly in the past, impact the pricing of raw materials and production costs and could have negative impacts on our operating margins.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Manufacturing cost performance also depends on volume absorption and capacity readiness; in the third quarter of 2026, Transportation Solutions cost of sales rose $74.5 million on $76.7 million higher material costs, $4.9 million higher labor costs, and accelerated dry van readiness spending, while low truck body volumes caused inefficiencies.
quotes: TS segment cost of sales was $403.9 million in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $74.5 million, or 22.6%, compared to the prior year period.
The increase in cost of sales was primarily attributable to increases of approximately $76.7 million in material costs and $4.9 million in labor costs, as well as other production-readiness costs.
Truck body profitability was affected by unfavorable customer mix and manufacturing inefficiencies associated with low production volumes.
In addition, during the third quarter of 2026, we incurred labor, onboarding, and other production-readiness costs to prepare our dry van operations for higher anticipated production levels in 2027.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Risk Factors, Q3 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A, and Q3 2026 earnings release non-GAAP reconciliation table.
business_model.claim: Footprint restructuring and network expansion initiatives also move costs, with 5,097 (table in thousands) of facility idling and related costs in the first nine months of 2026 from closing Little Falls and Goshen plants, plus higher lease, depreciation, maintenance, and start-up costs from expanding Parts & Services locations.
quotes: We also announced and initiated a plan to idle the facilities in Little Falls, Minnesota and in Goshen, Indiana, which includes job reductions and closures expected to be substantially complete by the end of the second fiscal quarter of 2026.
These increases, as well as other start-up costs, were largely associated with integrating new locations and expanding our Parts & Services network.
GAAP operating loss amounted to $20 million as the company recognized a $7.5 million gain on the sale of a manufacturing facility and recorded $0.5 million of facility idling costs.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
business_model.claim: For most truck bodies, Wabash installs bodies onto dealer- or end-user-owned chassis rather than holding chassis inventory, but must pay finance or storage charges if pooled chassis are not delivered within a specified timeframe.
quotes: With the exception of some specialty vehicle products, we generally do not purchase vehicle chassis for our inventory and accept shipments of vehicle chassis owned by dealers or end-users for the purpose of installing and/or manufacturing our specialized truck bodies on such chassis.
Under the converter chassis pool agreements, if a chassis is not delivered to a customer within a specified time frame, we must pay finance or storage charges on such chassis.

business_model.basis: Stated directly in the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Statements of Operations and MD&A.
business_model.claim: Below gross profit, Wabash incurs selling, general and administrative expenses, acquisition-related intangible amortization, and interest expense—which totaled $7.0 million in the third quarter of 2026—on its Senior Notes, Revolving Credit Agreement, and Convertible Notes.
quotes: Interest expense totaled $7.0 million during the third quarter of 2026 and $5.4 million during the third quarter of 2025.
Interest expense relates to interest and non-cash accretion charges on our Senior Notes, Revolving Credit Agreement, and Convertible Notes.
Amortization of intangibles was the result of expenses recognized for intangible assets recorded from previous acquisitions.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1 as management's belief
competitive_position.claim: Wabash positions itself as a leader in transportation, logistics, and infrastructure solutions through longstanding customer relationships, broad first-to-final mile product lines, engineering leadership, and an extensive dealer and partner network.
quotes: We believe our position as a leader in our key industries is the result of longstanding relationships with our core customers, our demonstrated ability to attract new customers, our broad and innovative product lines, our engineering leadership, and our extensive dealer and preferred partner network.

competitive_position.claim: In trailer manufacturing, Wabash competes on product quality, customer relationships, innovative technology, and price, while in truck bodies it operates as a national competitor alongside a few national peers and many smaller regional companies.
quotes: Trailer manufacturers compete primarily through the quality of their products, customer relationships, innovative technology, and price.
The truck body component of our Transportation Solutions segment competes in the specialized vehicle industry, whereby there are only a few national competitors and many smaller, regional companies.

competitive_position.claim: Wabash's quality tracking provides supporting evidence for its product reliability, with early lifecycle warranty claims averaging approximately 2.5, 2.8, and 2.6 units per 100 van trailers shipped in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
quotes: Using a unit-based warranty reporting process to track performance and document failure rates, early lifecycle warranty units per 100 van trailers shipped averaged approximately 2.5, 2.8, and 2.6 units in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

competitive_position.claim: Recent demand evidence shows third quarter 2026 net sales increased 24.8% year-over-year to $476.4 million as new trailer shipments rose 43.3% to 9,563 units, and total backlog reached approximately $1,198 million as of September 30, 2026.
quotes: The Company's net sales for the third quarter of 2026 were $476.4 million, reflecting a 24.8% increase compared to the same quarter of the previous year.

New trailers shipped during the third quarter of 2026 totaled 9,563 trailers compared to 6,675 trailers in the prior year period, an increase of 43.3%, which was primarily driven by higher dry van and platform shipments partially offset by lower tank trailer shipments.
As of September 30, 2026, total Company backlog stood at approximately $1,198 million, an increase of $242 million over the prior quarter.

competitive_position.claim: Customer demand led Wabash to accelerate dry van capacity-readiness activities from early 2027 into 2026 to support anticipated higher production in 2027.
quotes: A portion of the increase in labor costs, together with other production-readiness costs, reflected activities undertaken to prepare our dry van operations for higher anticipated production levels in 2027, including certain activities accelerated into 2026 from early 2027.

competitive_position.claim: Parts & Services provides a higher-margin revenue stream than equipment manufacturing, generating $69.4 million in third quarter 2026 net sales (up 13.8%) and a 15.7% gross profit margin versus Transportation Solutions' 1.0% gross profit margin and $7.5 million operating loss.
quotes: Parts & Services' net sales for the third quarter were $69.4 million, an increase of 13.8% compared to the prior year quarter.
Operating loss for the quarter amounted to $7.5 million, representing 1.8% of sales.

competitive_position.claim: Consolidated gross profit fell to $14,875 (table in thousands), or 3.1% of net sales, in the third quarter of 2026 despite higher revenue, showing limited near-term pricing power against unfavorable material costs and manufacturing inefficiencies.
quotes: Gross profit as a percentage of net sales was 3.1% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 4.1% for the same period in 2025.

The decrease in gross profit despite higher revenue was primarily attributable to lower trailer and truck body profitability resulting from unfavorable material costs and higher manufacturing costs, including labor and overhead.

competitive_position.claim: Competitors have introduced composite sidewalls that compete directly with Wabash's DuraPlate® products, and patents expiring from 2025 to 2045 may not prevent rivals from developing similar products or copying Wabash's technology.
quotes: We have observed others in the industry also pursue the development and use of composite sidewalls that compete directly with our DuraPlate® products.

We hold U.S. and foreign utility and design patents and patent applications on various components and techniques utilized in our manufacturing of transportation equipment and products with expiration dates ranging from 2025 to 2045.

If competitors are able to use our technology, our ability to effectively compete could be harmed and this could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: Unfairly traded van-type trailer imports from China, Canada, and Mexico threaten domestic production and pricing; while U.S. antidumping and countervailing duty orders cover China, investigations on Canada and Mexico remain pending and enforcement or circumvention risks persist.
quotes: Imports subject to these proceedings have adversely affected, and may continue to adversely affect, the U.S. trailer industry, including domestic production, shipments, performance and employment.
The investigations concerning imports from Canada and Mexico remain pending.

The failure or inability of U.S. trade officials to implement or effectively enforce antidumping and countervailing duty orders, or the modification, revocation, circumvention or avoidance of such orders, could permit unfairly traded imports to continue entering the United States and could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: A continuing freight recession in 2026—with ACT and FTR forecasting U.S. trailer production decreases of 6.6% and 7.7% after drops of 16.6% and 15.2% in 2025—alongside industry over-capacity and regional truck body rivals creates pricing pressure.
quotes: The most recent estimates from industry forecasters ACT Research Co. (“ACT”) and FTR Associates (“FTR”) indicate total United States trailer production levels for 2025 of approximately 196,000 and 195,000, respectively, which represents a decrease of approximately 16.6% and 15.2%, respectively, from 2024 production levels.

Current estimates from ACT and FTR for 2026 United States trailer production are 183,000 and 180,000, respectively, representing a decrease of approximately 6.6% and a decrease of 7.7%, respectively, versus 2025.

Manufacturing over-capacity and some of our competitors’ high leverage, along with bankruptcies, economic downturn and financial stresses that affected the industry, have in the past contributed, and may in the future contribute to significant pricing pressures.

Specialized vehicles are produced by a number of smaller, regional companies which create product pricing pressures that could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: Wabash faces customer concentration risk because its largest customers accounted for approximately 35% of aggregate net sales in 2025 (with no individual customer above 10%) and it lacks long-term agreements with all large customers.
quotes: Furthermore, we are subject to a concentration of risk as our five largest customers together accounted for approximately 35% of our aggregate net sales in 2025.
No individual customer accounted for more than 10% of our aggregate net sales in 2025 and international sales accounted for less than 10% in 2025.

competitive_position.claim: Dependence on a limited number of raw material and component suppliers and on GM, Freightliner, International, and Ford for customer-owned truck chassis exposes Wabash to supply disruptions, allocations, and chassis storage or finance charges.
quotes: We currently rely on a limited number of suppliers for raw materials and key components in the manufacturing of our products, such as tires, landing gear, axles, suspensions, specialty steel coil, stainless steel, plastic, aluminum and lumber.

Historically, General Motors Company (“GM”), Freightliner Custom Chassis (“Freightliner”), International Truck (“International”), and Ford Motor Company (“Ford”) have been the primary chassis suppliers.

competitive_position.claim: Wabash's strategic expansion faces execution threats as a recent entrant in trailer leasing (TaaS℠), in realizing expected returns from Wabash Parts LLC and wholly owned Linq Venture Holdings LLC, and from competitors potentially adopting artificial intelligence faster.
quotes: We face significant risks and challenges to our business and prospects as a recent entrant into the leasing and subleasing industry, including, among other things, our ability to design and build long-lived products that are aligned with freight leasing customer needs and changes in legislation and regulations in the various markets in which we operate, and cost-effectively maintain and repair our fleet to maximize our products’ economic life and the proceeds we receive from product sales.

If we are not able to successfully complete our parts and services distribution strategy, the anticipated enhanced revenue, earnings and cash flows resulting from this joint venture may not be realized fully or may take longer to realize than expected.

Our competitors or other third parties may incorporate artificial intelligence into their businesses more quickly or more successfully than us, which could result in reputational harm and could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.
